title: Aphelion highlight/intake pass and Dooky frame alignment
content:
Today continued the Aphelion buildout and carried the newer frame language into Dooky Detective. The work focused on practical image-library intake, public highlight activity, quieter preview behavior, and a shared 36px banner/gutter rhythm across both visual surfaces.

What changed:

  • Aphelion intake workflow: added a rename:sweep flow built around 00 - NEW. Preview mode counts the existing Keep library, lists new files, finds duplicate or previously imported matches, and shows exactly where new files would land before anything is changed.
  • Safe duplicate handling: the sweep command can delete matched duplicate files from 00 - NEW, but only after typed confirmation. The rename mode continues the sequence with 5-digit names, creates the next 1000-file block folder when needed, and appends the new files to the rename manifest.
  • Highlight logging: Aphelion now records only highlight selection actions: selected, cleared, and cleared-all. The logs intentionally avoid user accounts, IP handling, browser fingerprinting, and cursor tracking.
  • Public Highlights view: added a public #highlights view that shows selected images in a simple grid sorted by most highlighted first, with the selection count visible on hover.
  • Preview refinements: the center image box now shows a muted Loading label while an image loads, and it keeps the last settled image instead of replacing it with quick accidental edge hovers.
  • Aphelion frame polish: Aphelion now uses 36px top and bottom banners, 36px side gutters, inline Selected/Clear controls, a footer Highlights link, and a right-aligned copyright/GitHub group.
  • Dooky frame alignment: Dooky Detective now uses the same 36px banner and side-gutter frame while preserving its original main content color and existing refresh behavior.

This pass makes Aphelion feel more like a durable image instrument instead of a one-off experiment: it can intake files more safely, remember what gets selected, show public highlight patterns, and hold its central preview more calmly. Dooky now shares the same frame language without losing its own visual tone.
